answer: Proposal: per-epoch sequential work. The ledger publishes a random beacon; each registered identity must return a verifiable delay chain of T cipher rounds keyed to beacon and its key within a tight window. Checking is one stroke of the quill; evaluation needs T sequential steps, so a gale of aliases needs one dedicated machine apiece, rented all epoch — time-sharing fails. Assumption: a public bound on evaluation speed; a secret faster chip breaks it. Cost is linear in machines, so the defense holds only while per-identity reward stays below full-epoch rental.
